conventions.convention: Complex affine algebraic groups are nonempty; acted-on affine algebraic sets may be empty or reducible. Coordinate algebras and algebra maps are unital, with the zero algebra allowed.
The left action on functions is inverse pullback: (g f)(x)=f(g⁻¹x). Its right coaction lands in A⊗H; direct action pullback lands in H⊗A and evaluates to f(gx).

A rational module requires finite-dimensional stable subspaces with algebraic action, not merely finite-dimensional spans of abstract orbits. Torus function weights are opposite point-coordinate weights.

A group variety is smooth, separated and finite type. An abelian variety is a proper geometrically connected group variety; projectivity and commutativity are conclusions. Pseudo-abelian means smooth connected with no nontrivial smooth connected affine normal subgroup, without assuming properness.

Normal quotients represent fppf sheafified cosets, have faithfully flat finitely presented torsor projections, and use scheme-theoretic kernels. Nonsmooth and nonreduced subgroup schemes are retained.
Faithfulness and stabilizers are tested on all test schemes or all k-algebras, including nonreduced algebras; faithfulness on rational points is insufficient.

Perfect-field Barsotti–Chevalley asserts a unique smooth connected affine normal kernel for a smooth connected source. The arbitrary-field theorem asserts existence with a possibly nonsmooth connected affine kernel and makes no uniqueness claim.
Degree is measured over the stated ground field: deg_C(L)=χ_k(C,L)−χ_k(C,O_C), on proper schemes of dimension at most one, including empty, reducible and nonreduced schemes.

The surface is integral, regular, projective and pure dimension two over an arbitrary field. The line-bundle pairing is χ(O_X)−χ(L∨)−χ(M∨)+χ(L∨⊗M∨); divisors are Cartier. Geometric smoothness is not required.

For a closed blowup centre p, r=[κ(p):k], E≅P¹_κ(p), and E²=−r. Strict-transform formulas use the order m of the local equation and retain the factors mr and m²r; no residue-field separability is assumed.

AC is explicitly inherited by the affine reconstruction, regularity, descent, cohomology and surface arguments. The cube, multiplication and ensuing structure theorems explicitly assume AC and DC; the finite-coefficient comodule arguments declare themselves choice-free.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC. For a separated finite-type group scheme G over a field and a closed normal subgroup scheme H, the fppf sheafified coset functor is represented by a separated finite-type group scheme Q=G/H. The projection is faithfully flat of finite presentation, has scheme kernel H, and (g,h)↦(g,gh) identifies G×H with G×_QG. It is universal for homomorphisms killing H and commutes with field extension. Connectedness and smoothness of G pass to Q; smoothness of H makes the projection smooth. Existence does not require H reduced or smooth.
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Every regular local ring is a unique factorization domain. In particular every smooth finite-type scheme over a field is locally factorial.
Assume the Axiom of Choice. A smooth geometrically integral separated finite-type group scheme G over any field k has an ample invertible sheaf.

Assume AC. Let X be proper geometrically integral of finite type over k with x₀∈X(k), Y connected of finite type, and Z separated of finite type. If f:X×Y→Z is constant on X×{y₀} for some y₀∈Y(k), then f=f(x₀,−)∘pr_Y.

Assume AC. Over an algebraically closed field, exactly one holds for a smooth connected algebraic group G: G is proper, hence an abelian variety; or G contains a positive-dimensional smooth connected affine closed subgroup. Every nonproper smooth algebraic group, including a disconnected one, contains such a subgroup in its identity component.

Assume AC and DC. For an abelian variety A over any field and an invertible sheaf L, m₁₂₃*L⊗m₁*L⊗m₂*L⊗m₃*L≅m₁₂*L⊗m₁₃*L⊗m₂₃*L. More generally, an invertible sheaf on A³ trivial on the first two identity faces and on A×A×{z} for one point z is trivial; the last fibre's triviality is over κ(z).

Assume AC and DC. For an abelian variety A of dimension g over any field and a nonzero integer n, [n]:A→A is finite faithfully flat and locally free of constant rank |n|^(2g). Its scheme kernel has that rank, including when the characteristic divides n. Every scheme-valued point becomes divisible by n after a finite faithfully flat cover; rational points over an algebraically closed field are divisible.

Assume AC. For a proper k-scheme C of dimension at most one and invertible sheaves L,M, deg_C(L⊗M)=deg_C(L)+deg_C(M), deg_C(L∨)=−deg_C(L), and χ(L⊗M)−χ(L)−χ(M)+χ(O_C)=0. C need not be reduced, irreducible or normal.

Assume AC. On an integral regular projective surface over a field, (L⊗M)·N=L·N+M·N and L·(M⊗N)=L·M+L·N. The pairing on Pic(X) is symmetric and Z-bilinear and vanishes against O_X; equivalently the Cartier-divisor pairing is symmetric and additive in each variable.

Assume AC. Blowing up a closed point p of an integral regular projective surface gives an integral regular projective surface with effective Cartier exceptional curve E≅P¹_κ(p), O_E(E)≅O(−1), and E²=−[κ(p):k]. For Cartier D,D′, E·π*D=0 and π*D·π*D′=D·D′. For a reduced effective Cartier C through p of multiplicity m≥1, π*C=C′+mE, C′·E=m[κ(p):k], and (C′)²=C²−m²[κ(p):k]. If p∉C, π*C=C′ and (C′)²=C².

Assume AC through the affine Nullstellensatz and morphism dictionary. Every algebraic action of a complex affine algebraic group G on an affine algebraic set X has a finite-dimensional rational submodule W⊂C[X] generating C[X], such that evaluation X→W* is an equivariant isomorphism onto a closed invariant algebraic subset. The dual action is (gλ)(w)=λ(g⁻¹w). Connectedness, irreducibility and reductivity are not required.

concerns.concern: F1 cites def-abelian-variety-over-a-field for the general group-scheme/Hopf interface, but that Definition introduces smooth group varieties. The nonsmooth interface is available in the prerequisite page's def-group-scheme-over-a-field and def-morphism-and-closed-subgroup-scheme, yet neither is cited or declared here. The same citation issue occurs in thm-nonaffine-group-scheme-normal-subgroup-quotient F1. The formal arguments retain nonsmooth schemes correctly; reconcile the foundational item citations/dependencies and applicable cross-batch ledger rather than narrowing the claims.

alerts.finding: The current item correctly says 'if f is a k-morphism', but its entry in research/frontier-38-owner-30-batch-2.pages.json still says 'if X and Y are proper over a field k' and asserts χ(X,f*L)=χ(Y,L) under the structure-sheaf pushforward hypotheses without requiring a k-morphism. That manifest claim is false: take k=F_p(t), X=Spec k with its identity structural map, Y=Spec k with structural map t↦t^p, f the identity of the underlying schemes, and L=O_Y. Both structural maps are finite and proper; f_*O_X=O_Y and all higher direct images vanish, but χ_k(X,O_X)=1 and χ_k(Y,O_Y)=p. The source item and our blowup consumer are already qualified correctly. This is the manifest discrepancy still recorded open in batch 26's dependency ledger.
